title.narrative: Provision of essential life-saving services to vulnerable children and women in the three regions affected by the impact of El Niño-induced drought in Kavango East, Kavango West, Omaheke, Namibia

description.narrative: The estimated humanitarian need for the three regions is USD 3,126, 630 million, of which 1,200,000 million is being requested through CERF to support affected communities in all the three Kavango East, Kavango West, and Omaheke regions. A USD 100,000 has been mobilized by time of this submission. The country will adopt an integrated approach for all complementary nutrition sensitive and specific actions that will enhance coverage, timeliness, and effectiveness of response to reduce morbidity and mortality risk associated with this drought emergency. A standard government-led package of services will be implemented in all service delivery points using the existing health care system. The government will take lead in the coordination of the response in complementing the actions by other UN agencies and partners by leveraging existing technical and financial resources to sustain this partnership.The integrated WASH, Health and nutrition response will ensure that gender, protection, disability issues are mainstreamed in programming across the sectors. Women and men, boys and girls, and people with disabilities will be indirectly engaged throughout the implementation process while considering sociocultural contexts and unique challenges and barriers that affect them. Through targeted activities including training, social mobilization, and counselling, their knowledge, and skill gained will improve their well-being. Through community engagements, the project will ensure that voices of women are heard, and the environment is conducive to women speaking without discrimination or intimidation. Where agreeable, joint sessions will be held to address issues of stigma and encourage the empowerment and inclusion of women and girls in leadership and decision making. Equal opportunity will also be assured for everyone regardless of their gender and diversity in the emergency response activity package. During community activities such as the community support groups, community dialogues/meetings, both men and women will collaborate for mutual benefit. Considering the importance of GBV prevention and response interventions and child protection, UNICEF, government, and partner staff will be refreshed on protection principles, human rights, safeguarding strategies, including PSEA, and inclusivity to ensure safe programming. To ensure transparency occurs, feedback complaints and response mechanisms will also be shared with the community as they become aware of their rights, responsibilities, and potential options in the event of rights violation. The use of UReport as feedback mechanism and also information sharing platform will be applied.
